📝
Day Before

☐ Review Ch 36 (Exam Strategy) and Ch 38 (Last-Mile Review). ☐ Memorize the 15 critical file paths. ☐ Practice the context switch ritual 10 times. ☐ Prepare your workspace: clear desk, good lighting, quiet room with closed door. ☐ Charge laptop. ☐ Set alarm 2+ hours before exam.

🪪
Morning Of

☐ Wake up 2+ hours before. Eat a proper meal. ☐ Government-issued photo ID ready (passport or driver's license). ☐ Clear desk completely — no papers, no phone, no second screen. ☐ Webcam positioned to show your face and hands. ☐ Do a 10-minute terminal warmup.

🧠
30 Minutes Before

☐ Launch PSI Secure Browser. ☐ Begin check-in process. ☐ Show ID to webcam. ☐ Pan webcam around the room (all 4 walls, desk surface, UNDER desk). ☐ Proctor verifies your environment. ☐ Mentally recite: "kubectl config use-context, kubectl config current-context, kubectl get nodes."

✅
Exam Start

☐ Terminal appears. ☐ Read Task 1. ☐ Copy context switch command. ☐ kubectl config use-context <name>. ☐ kubectl config current-context (verify). ☐ Solve the task. ☐ Mark done in notepad. ☐ Repeat for all tasks. ☐ 3-pass strategy: Easy → Medium → Hard + Verify.

⚡ Exam Day Mental Warmup — 10 Commands to Type Before You Start

During the check-in waiting period (proctor is verifying other candidates), you can't use the terminal but you CAN mentally rehearse. Recite these 10 commands:

Bash — Mental warmup: recite these in order before the exam starts
# 1. Context switch (THE RITUAL — do this for EVERY task)
kubectl config use-context <name>
kubectl config current-context

# 2. Quick pod with security context
kubectl run test --image=nginx --restart=Never --dry-run=client -o yaml | vi -

# 3. RBAC creation (NEVER write YAML from scratch)
kubectl create role r1 --verb=get,list --resource=pods -n ns --dry-run=client -o yaml

# 4. RBAC verification
kubectl auth can-i get pods -n ns --as=system:serviceaccount:ns:sa

# 5. NetworkPolicy test
kubectl run test --rm -it --image=busybox --restart=Never -- wget -qO- --timeout=5 <url>

# 6. Falco rules — always edit LOCAL file
vi /etc/falco/falco_rules.local.yaml

# 7. Trivy scan
trivy image --severity CRITICAL,HIGH <image>

# 8. API server edit — add BOTH flag AND volume mount
vi /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml

# 9. etcd verification
ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 \
  --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt \
  --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.crt \
  --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.key \
  get /registry/secrets/ns/name | hexdump -C

# 10. Namespace PSS label
kubectl label ns <name> pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=restricted

🔄 Retake Strategy — What to Do If You Don't Pass

1Review Your Score Report

The Linux Foundation provides a domain-by-domain breakdown of your performance. Identify which domains you scored lowest in. Focus your retake preparation on those domains specifically.

2Analyze What Went Wrong

Did you run out of time? (Practice speed drills.) Did you forget context switching? (Build the ritual habit.) Did you not know the commands? (Review Appendix A and practice labs.) Were you anxious? (Practice under timed conditions more.)

3Retake Within 2-4 Weeks

Your free retake is valid for 12 months. Don't wait too long — the knowledge fades. Schedule your retake 2-4 weeks after the failed attempt. Focus study on weak domains, not re-reading everything.

4What's Different on Retake

The retake exam has different tasks but the same format and domains. The environment is identical. Your previous exam experience is an advantage — you know exactly what to expect.

Weekly Study Routine — How to Structure Each Week

📖Days 1-2: Read (2-3 hours)

Read the assigned chapters. Don't just skim — understand every code block and diagram. Write down questions. Highlight commands you'll need to memorize. Focus on the "Why" behind each security control, not just the "What."

💻Days 3-5: Lab (4-6 hours)

Do the hands-on lab for the week. Use a real cluster (minikube, kind, or cloud sandbox). Type every command — don't copy-paste. If something doesn't work, debug it. The bugs you fix during practice are the bugs you'll fix FAST on the exam.

🔄Day 6: Review (1-2 hours)

Re-read the chapters with fresh eyes after the lab. The concepts will click differently after hands-on experience. Review any commands that were difficult in the lab. Update your personal cheat sheet.

🧠Day 7: Flashcards (1 hour)

Create flashcards for the week's key commands and file paths. Quiz yourself. The goal is RECALL, not recognition — can you type the command from memory? Practice until the commands flow from muscle memory.

💡 Study Tips for CKS Success

1. Consistency beats cramming: 1 hour every day is more effective than 7 hours on Saturday. Your brain consolidates learning during sleep. 2. Lab every concept: Reading about NetworkPolicy is not the same as applying one and testing it. Every chapter's lab is mandatory. 3. Teach someone: Explain what you learned to a colleague (or your rubber duck). Teaching reveals gaps in understanding. 4. Time everything: From Week 6 onward, time every lab task. Speed comes from repetition, not understanding. 5. Simulate exam conditions: In Weeks 9-10, practice in a quiet room with only kubernetes.io and falco.org open. No notes, no phone, 2-hour timer.

🧪 Appendix H: Hands-On Lab Workbook — The 95%+ Gap Filler

This appendix is the bridge between knowledge and performance. The CKS exam is not a quiz — it's a timed, performance-based test on live clusters. Every exercise below is designed to be executed on a real cluster (kind, minikube, Killercoda, or your own). Each lab includes: time limit (exam-realistic), step-by-step solution, and verification check. Complete all 56 exercises across 6 domains, then attempt the 2-hour Timed Mock Exam at the end. If you score 90%+ on the mock, you're ready for 95%+ on the real thing.

🧪 56+ Labs ⏱️ ~30 hours 🏗️ Hands-On 🎯 95%+ Target

📊 Lab Scoring Rubric

ScoreCriteria
100%Completed within time limit, all verifications pass, no hints used
75%Completed within 1.5× time limit, all verifications pass
50%Completed but needed hints or exceeded time limit
0%Could not complete, or verification fails

🏗️ Domain 1: Cluster Setup — 10 Labs (CKS 15%)

Focus: NetworkPolicy, RBAC, TLS, Dashboard security, etcd backup/restore, cluster upgrades. These labs build the foundational muscle memory for 15% of the exam.

Lab 1.1
⏱️ 10 min — NetworkPolicy: Default-Deny + DNS + App Rules
Create namespace secure-lab. Apply a default-deny-all NetworkPolicy. Then add rules allowing: (a) DNS from CoreDNS, (b) ingress to pods labeled app: web from pods labeled app: gateway on port 8080, (c) egress from app: web to app: db on port 5432. Verify connectivity works ONLY for allowed paths.
Show Solution
Solution
kubectl create ns secure-lab
# Default-deny
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata: {name: default-deny, namespace: secure-lab}
spec: {podSelector: {}, policyTypes: [Ingress, Egress]}
EOF
# DNS allow
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata: {name: allow-dns, namespace: secure-lab}
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes: [Egress]
  egress:
  - to: [{namespaceSelector: {matchLabels: {kubernetes.io/metadata.name: kube-system}}, podSelector: {k8s-app: kube-dns}}]
    ports: [{protocol: UDP, port: 53}]
EOF
# Run test pods and verify
Lab 1.2
⏱️ 8 min — RBAC: Least Privilege for CI/CD
Create SA cicd-bot in staging namespace. Grant ONLY: get/list/watch/update/patch on Deployments, create/update Secrets. No other permissions. Verify with kubectl auth can-i that it CAN update deployments but CANNOT delete pods or list secrets.
Show Solution
Solution
kubectl create ns staging
kubectl create sa cicd-bot -n staging
kubectl create role cicd-deployer -n staging --verb=get,list,watch,update,patch --resource=deployments
kubectl create rolebinding cicd-bind --role=cicd-deployer --serviceaccount=staging:cicd-bot -n staging
kubectl auth can-i update deployments --as=system:serviceaccount:staging:cicd-bot -n staging
kubectl auth can-i delete pods --as=system:serviceaccount:staging:cicd-bot -n staging  # MUST be "no"
Lab 1.3
⏱️ 12 min — etcd Backup & Restore
Take an etcd snapshot. Create a Secret. Delete the Secret. Restore etcd from the snapshot. Verify the Secret is back. Time includes snapshot, restore, and verification.
Show Solution
Solution
ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.crt --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.key snapshot save /tmp/backup.db
kubectl create secret generic test-backup --from-literal=k=v
kubectl delete secret test-backup
mv /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml /tmp/
ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot restore /tmp/backup.db --data-dir=/var/lib/etcd-restored
# Edit etcd.yaml to point --data-dir=/var/lib/etcd-restored
mv /tmp/kube-apiserver.yaml /etc/kubernetes/manifests/
kubectl get secret test-backup  # MUST exist
Lab 1.4
⏱️ 10 min — Cluster Upgrade Simulation
Given cluster v1.29.x, upgrade the control plane to v1.30.x. Then upgrade kubelet on one worker. Verify all nodes show Ready with new version. Take etcd snapshot BEFORE upgrade.
Show Solution
Solution
ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot save /tmp/pre-upgrade.db
apt-mark unhold kubeadm && apt-get update && apt-get install -y kubeadm=1.30.x-00 && apt-mark hold kubeadm
kubeadm upgrade plan
kubeadm upgrade apply v1.30.x
kubectl drain worker01 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
apt-get install -y kubelet=1.30.x-00 kubectl=1.30.x-00
systemctl restart kubelet && kubectl uncordon worker01
kubectl get nodes  # All Ready, all v1.30.x
Lab 1.5
⏱️ 6 min — TLS Secret + Ingress
Generate a self-signed TLS cert for lab.anihpj.com. Create TLS Secret lab-tls. Create an Ingress that uses this Secret for TLS termination. Curl the endpoint with --resolve to verify TLS works.
Show Solution
Solution
openssl req -x509 -nodes -days 365 -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout lab.key -out lab.crt -subj "/CN=lab.anihpj.com"
kubectl create secret tls lab-tls --cert=lab.crt --key=lab.key -n default
kubectl create ingress lab-tls --class=nginx --rule="lab.anihpj.com/*=web-svc:80,tls=lab-tls"
curl -k --resolve lab.anihpj.com:443:<INGRESS-IP> https://lab.anihpj.com
Lab 1.6
⏱️ 8 min — ServiceAccount Zero-Privilege Setup
Create SA no-api with automountServiceAccountToken: false. Create a pod using this SA. Verify: (a) /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token does NOT exist, (b) kubectl auth can-i --as=system:serviceaccount:default:no-api get pods returns "no".
Show Solution
Solution
kubectl create sa no-api
kubectl patch sa no-api -p '{"automountServiceAccountToken": false}'
kubectl run test --image=busybox --restart=Never --command -- sleep 300 --serviceaccount=no-api
kubectl exec test -- ls /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/  # MUST fail
kubectl auth can-i get pods --as=system:serviceaccount:default:no-api  # MUST return "no"
Lab 1.7
⏱️ 10 min — Dashboard Security Audit
Deploy Kubernetes Dashboard in namespace kubernetes-dashboard. Ensure: (a) --enable-skip-login is NOT set, (b) Dashboard SA has NO cluster-admin, (c) Dashboard Service is ClusterIP (not LoadBalancer), (d) NetworkPolicy restricts ingress to dashboard pod.
Show Solution
Solution
kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kubernetes/dashboard/v2.7.0/aio/deploy/recommended.yaml
kubectl get deploy kubernetes-dashboard -n kubernetes-dashboard -o yaml | grep skip-login
kubectl auth can-i --list -n kubernetes-dashboard --as=system:serviceaccount:kubernetes-dashboard:kubernetes-dashboard | grep -v "\[\]"
kubectl get svc kubernetes-dashboard -n kubernetes-dashboard  # Must be ClusterIP
kubectl apply -f dashboard-networkpolicy.yaml  # Restrict ingress
Lab 1.8
⏱️ 5 min — Anonymous Access Verification
Verify anonymous access is disabled on the API server. Test with curl WITHOUT credentials. Then check the flag in the API server manifest.
Show Solution
Solution
curl -k https://localhost:6443/api  # Must return 401 Unauthorized
grep anonymous-auth /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml  # Must show --anonymous-auth=false
Lab 1.9
⏱️ 7 min — ClusterRole vs Role: Cross-Namespace Access
Create ClusterRole pod-reader (get/list pods). Create RoleBinding in ns1 to SA reader in ns2. Verify SA can read pods in ns1 but NOT in ns2.
Show Solution
Solution
kubectl create clusterrole pod-reader --verb=get,list --resource=pods
kubectl create ns ns1 && kubectl create ns ns2
kubectl create sa reader -n ns2
kubectl create rolebinding pod-reader-ns1 --clusterrole=pod-reader --serviceaccount=ns2:reader -n ns1
kubectl auth can-i get pods --as=system:serviceaccount:ns2:reader -n ns1  # yes
kubectl auth can-i get pods --as=system:serviceaccount:ns2:reader -n ns2  # no
Lab 1.10
⏱️ 8 min — API Server Flag Audit
SSH to control plane. List ALL security-relevant API server flags. Identify: authorization-mode, anonymous-auth, enable-admission-plugins. If any are missing or insecure (e.g., AlwaysAllow), fix them. Verify the API server restarts successfully.
Show Solution
Solution
cat /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml | grep -E "authorization-mode|anonymous-auth|enable-admission-plugins"
# Expected: --authorization-mode=Node,RBAC --anonymous-auth=false --enable-admission-plugins=NodeRestriction,...
kubectl get nodes  # Verify API server is healthy after changes

🛡️ Domain 2: Cluster Hardening — 10 Labs (CKS 15%)

Focus: CIS benchmarks, kube-bench, RBAC, admission controllers, PSP/PSS migration, NodeRestriction, audit logging. These are the most common exam tasks.

Lab 2.1
⏱️ 12 min — Run kube-bench & Fix All FAILs
Run kube-bench as a Job against the master node. Identify every [FAIL]. Fix at least 5 FAILs: anonymous-auth, authorization-mode, audit-log-path, profiling, and one more. Re-run kube-bench to verify all former FAILs are now PASS.
Show Solution
Solution
kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aquasecurity/kube-bench/main/job.yaml
kubectl logs job/kube-bench | grep FAIL
# Fix each FAIL in /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml
# Wait for restart, re-run kube-bench
kubectl delete job kube-bench && kubectl apply -f ...job.yaml
kubectl logs job/kube-bench | grep FAIL  # Should be empty or only informational
Lab 2.2
⏱️ 8 min — Kubelet Hardening
Edit /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml: disable anonymous-auth, set authorization-mode to Webhook, disable readOnlyPort (set to 0), enable protectKernelDefaults. Restart kubelet and verify with kube-bench node checks.
Show Solution
Solution
vi /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml
# Set: authentication.anonymous.enabled: false, authorization.mode: Webhook, readOnlyPort: 0, protectKernelDefaults: true
systemctl restart kubelet
kube-bench run --targets node --check 4.2.1,4.2.2,4.2.3,4.2.6
Lab 2.3
⏱️ 10 min — Enable NodeRestriction Admission Plugin
Verify NodeRestriction is in the admission plugins list. If not, add it. Test: kubelet on worker01 should NOT be able to modify worker02's labels. Verify with kubectl auth can-i.
Show Solution
Solution
grep enable-admission-plugins /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml
# Add NodeRestriction if missing. Wait for restart.
kubectl auth can-i update nodes/worker02 --as=system:node:worker01  # MUST be "no"
Lab 2.4
⏱️ 10 min — Audit Policy: Secrets + RBAC Logging
Create an audit policy that logs: (a) all Secret operations at Metadata level, (b) all RBAC changes at RequestResponse level, (c) nothing else. Configure API server to use it. Create a test Secret and verify it appears in audit logs.
Show Solution
Solution
apiVersion: audit.k8s.io/v1
kind: Policy
rules:
- level: Metadata
  resources: [{group: "", resources: ["secrets"]}]
- level: RequestResponse
  resources: [{group: "rbac.authorization.k8s.io", resources: ["*"]}]
- level: None
Lab 2.5
⏱️ 6 min — SSH Hardening
On each node: disable root SSH login, disable password authentication, disable X11 forwarding. Restart SSH. Verify root can't SSH with password.
Show Solution
Solution
sed -i 's/^PermitRootLogin.*/PermitRootLogin no/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config
sed -i 's/^PasswordAuthentication.*/PasswordAuthentication no/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config
sed -i 's/^X11Forwarding.*/X11Forwarding no/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config
systemctl restart sshd
Lab 2.6
⏱️ 15 min — EncryptionConfiguration: Full Setup
Create EncryptionConfiguration for Secrets using aescbc. Update API server manifest with flag, volumeMount, AND volume. Restart. Verify by reading etcd directly — data must be encrypted with k8s:enc:aescbc prefix.
Show Solution
Solution
cat > /etc/kubernetes/encryption-config.yaml <<EOF
apiVersion: apiserver.config.k8s.io/v1
kind: EncryptionConfiguration
resources: [{resources: ["secrets"], providers: [{aescbc: {keys: [{name: key1, secret: $(head -c32 /dev/urandom | base64)}]}}, {identity: {}}]}]
EOF
# Edit kube-apiserver.yaml: add flag + volumeMount + volume
kubectl create secret generic test-enc --from-literal=k=v
ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl get /registry/secrets/default/test-enc | hexdump -C | head  # Must show k8s:enc:aescbc
Lab 2.7
⏱️ 8 min — RBAC Impersonation Audit
Create a user with impersonate permission. Impersonate another user. Check audit logs for the impersonation event — verify the original username is preserved.
Show Solution
Solution
kubectl create clusterrole impersonator --verb=impersonate --resource=users
kubectl create clusterrolebinding imp-bind --clusterrole=impersonator --user=auditor
kubectl get pods --as=system:admin  # Impersonate
cat /var/log/kubernetes/audit.log | jq 'select(.user.extra."authentication.k8s.io/original-username" != null)'
Lab 2.8
⏱️ 6 min — API Server Profiling Disable
Verify --profiling=false on API server, controller-manager, and scheduler. If enabled, disable it. Verify /debug/pprof/ returns 404 or 403.
Show Solution
Solution
grep profiling /etc/kubernetes/manifests/*.yaml
kubectl get --raw /debug/pprof/  # Must return 404 or empty
Lab 2.9
⏱️ 7 min — Static Pod Manifest Permission Fix
Verify permissions on /etc/kubernetes/manifests/*.yaml are 600 and owned by root:root. Fix any that aren't.
Show Solution
Solution
stat -c "%a %U:%G %n" /etc/kubernetes/manifests/*.yaml
chmod 600 /etc/kubernetes/manifests/*.yaml
chown root:root /etc/kubernetes/manifests/*.yaml
Lab 2.10
⏱️ 10 min — Audit Log Webhook Configuration
Configure audit log webhook to ship events to a mock endpoint. Create webhook kubeconfig. Verify API server has --audit-webhook-config-file flag. Check API server logs for successful webhook connection.
Show Solution
Solution
cat > /etc/kubernetes/audit-webhook.yaml <<EOF
apiVersion: v1; kind: Config; clusters: [{name: siem, cluster: {server: https://siem.anihpj.com:8088}}]
users: [{name: webhook, user: {token: test-token}}]
contexts: [{context: {cluster: siem, user: webhook}, name: audit}]
current-context: audit
EOF
# Add --audit-webhook-config-file=/etc/kubernetes/audit-webhook.yaml to API server

🔒 Domain 3: System Hardening — 8 Labs (CKS 10%)

Focus: AppArmor, Seccomp, kernel hardening, OS minimization. These labs require SSH access to nodes.

Lab 3.1
⏱️ 12 min — AppArmor: Write, Load, Apply, Test
Write an AppArmor profile that allows read of /app/**, write to /tmp/**, and denies access to /etc/kubernetes/. Load it with apparmor_parser. Apply to a pod. Test that the pod CAN read /app but CANNOT read /etc/kubernetes.
Show Solution
Solution
cat > /etc/apparmor.d/k8s-app <<EOF
profile k8s-app flags=(attach_disconnected) { #include <abstractions/base>  /app/** r,  /tmp/** rw,  deny /etc/kubernetes/** rw, }
EOF
apparmor_parser -q /etc/apparmor.d/k8s-app
kubectl run test --image=busybox --restart=Never --command -- sleep 300 --annotations="container.apparmor.security.beta.kubernetes.io/test: localhost/k8s-app"
kubectl exec test -- cat /etc/kubernetes/pki/ca.crt  # MUST fail "Permission denied"
Lab 3.2
⏱️ 10 min — Custom Seccomp Profile: Block mount + unshare
Write a Seccomp profile blocking mount, umount2, unshare, and reboot. Save to /var/lib/kubelet/seccomp/. Apply to pod. Verify pod starts and unshare is blocked.
Show Solution
Solution
cat > /var/lib/kubelet/seccomp/block-escape.json <<EOF
{"defaultAction":"SCMP_ACT_ALLOW","architectures":["SCMP_ARCH_X86_64"],"syscalls":[{"names":["mount","umount2","unshare","reboot","kexec_load"],"action":"SCMP_ACT_ERRNO"}]}
EOF
kubectl run secured --image=busybox --dry-run=client -o yaml | sed 's/containers:/securityContext:\n        seccompProfile: {type: Localhost, localhostProfile: block-escape.json}\n      containers:/' | kubectl apply -f -
Lab 3.3
⏱️ 8 min — Kernel Module Blacklisting
Blacklist: cramfs, freevxfs, jffs2, hfs, hfsplus, squashfs, udf. Verify with lsmod they're not loaded. Set modules_disabled after verification.
Show Solution
Solution
for mod in cramfs freevxfs jffs2 hfs hfsplus squashfs udf; do echo "blacklist $mod" >> /etc/modprobe.d/blacklist.conf; modprobe -r $mod 2>/dev/null; done
lsmod | grep -E "cramfs|freevxfs|jffs2|hfs|squashfs|udf"  # Should be empty
echo 1 > /proc/sys/kernel/modules_disabled  # Lock it
Lab 3.4
⏱️ 6 min — Port Minimization
SSH to worker node. List all listening ports. Identify non-Kubernetes services. Stop and disable: FTP, SMTP, NFS, CUPS, avahi. Verify only kubelet, containerd, and SSH remain.
Show Solution
Solution
ss -tulnp
systemctl stop vsftpd postfix nfs-server cups avahi-daemon 2>/dev/null
systemctl disable vsftpd postfix nfs-server cups avahi-daemon 2>/dev/null
ss -tulnp | grep -v -E "kubelet|containerd|sshd"  # Should be empty or minimal
Lab 3.5
⏱️ 8 min — AIDE: Initialize, Check, Update
Install AIDE. Initialize the database. Modify /etc/hosts (simulate tampering). Run aide --check and verify the modification is detected. Update the database after the "legitimate" change.
Show Solution
Solution
apt-get install -y aide
aide --init && cp /var/lib/aide/aide.db.new.gz /var/lib/aide/aide.db.gz
echo "10.0.0.50 bad.host.com" >> /etc/hosts  # Simulate tampering
aide --check  # Reports /etc/hosts changed
aide --update && cp /var/lib/aide/aide.db.new.gz /var/lib/aide/aide.db.gz  # Accept change
Lab 3.6
⏱️ 5 min — Kernel Hardening: sysctl Security Settings
Set: kernel.randomize_va_space=2, kernel.kptr_restrict=2, kernel.dmesg_restrict=1, net.ipv4.tcp_syncookies=1. Persist in /etc/sysctl.d/99-security.conf.
Show Solution
Solution
cat > /etc/sysctl.d/99-security.conf <<EOF
kernel.randomize_va_space=2
kernel.kptr_restrict=2
kernel.dmesg_restrict=1
net.ipv4.tcp_syncookies=1
net.ipv4.ip_forward=0
EOF
sysctl --system
Lab 3.7
⏱️ 6 min — Remove Unnecessary Packages
List all installed packages. Remove unnecessary ones: ftp, telnet, nfs-common, rpcbind, bluetooth, wireless-tools. Verify removed packages are gone.
Show Solution
Solution
apt list --installed | grep -E "ftp|telnet|nfs|rpcbind|bluetooth|wireless"
apt remove --purge ftp telnet nfs-common rpcbind bluetooth wireless-tools -y
Lab 3.8
⏱️ 10 min — Seccomp RuntimeDefault + Profile Debugging
Deploy a pod with RuntimeDefault Seccomp. If it crashes, debug which syscall is blocked (dmesg), create a custom profile allowing that syscall, and redeploy. Verify the pod runs.
Show Solution
Solution
kubectl run test --image=nginx --dry-run=client -o yaml | sed 's/containers:/securityContext:\n        seccompProfile: {type: RuntimeDefault}\n      containers:/' | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl logs test  # Check for errors
dmesg | grep -i seccomp  # Find blocked syscall
# Create custom profile allowing the blocked syscall, redeploy

🐳 Domain 4: Minimize Microservice Vulnerabilities — 10 Labs (CKS 20%)

Lab 4.1
⏱️ 8 min — PSS Restricted: Label + Fix Violations
Label namespace prod-lab with enforce=restricted. Deploy a pod running as root — it must be REJECTED. Fix the pod spec to satisfy Restricted (non-root, Seccomp, drop ALL caps, readOnlyRoot). Redeploy — must succeed.
Show Solution
Solution
kubectl create ns prod-lab
kubectl label ns prod-lab pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=restricted
kubectl label ns prod-lab pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce-version=v1.30
# Deploy root pod — REJECTED
kubectl run root-pod --image=nginx -n prod-lab  # FAILS
# Fix and redeploy with securityContext (runAsNonRoot, seccomp, drop ALL, readOnly)
Lab 4.2
⏱️ 7 min — Full SecurityContext Implementation
Deploy a pod with the CKS golden securityContext: runAsNonRoot:true, runAsUser:1000, allowPrivilegeEscalation:false, readOnlyRootFilesystem:true, capabilities.drop:[ALL], seccompProfile.type:RuntimeDefault. Add emptyDir for /tmp. Verify: can write to /tmp, cannot write to /etc.
Show Solution
Solution
securityContext:
  runAsNonRoot: true; runAsUser: 1000; allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true; capabilities: {drop: [ALL]}
  seccompProfile: {type: RuntimeDefault}
volumeMounts: [{name: tmp, mountPath: /tmp}]
volumes: [{name: tmp, emptyDir: {}}]
Lab 4.3
⏱️ 8 min — Secrets Encryption Verification
Create a Secret. Read it via kubectl (should show base64). Read it via etcdctl directly — must show encrypted data with k8s:enc prefix. If not encrypted, enable EncryptionConfiguration and retest.
Show Solution
Solution
kubectl create secret generic verify-enc --from-literal=password=SuperSecret123
kubectl get secret verify-enc -o jsonpath='{.data.password}' | base64 -d  # Shows plaintext
ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl get /registry/secrets/default/verify-enc | hexdump -C | head  # Must show k8s:enc
Lab 4.4
⏱️ 10 min — gVisor RuntimeClass: Setup + Apply
Install gVisor (or verify it's installed). Create RuntimeClass gvisor with handler runsc. Deploy a pod using this RuntimeClass. Verify with dmesg | grep gvisor or check /proc/1/cgroup inside the pod.
Show Solution
Solution
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: node.k8s.io/v1; kind: RuntimeClass; metadata: {name: gvisor}; handler: runsc
EOF
kubectl run sandboxed --image=nginx --overrides='{"spec":{"runtimeClassName":"gvisor"}}'
kubectl exec sandboxed -- dmesg | grep -i gvisor
Lab 4.5
⏱️ 8 min — Istio mTLS: STRICT Mode
Install Istio (or use existing). Label namespace mtls-test for injection. Deploy two pods. Apply PeerAuthentication STRICT. Verify mTLS is active with istioctl authn tls-check.
Show Solution
Solution
kubectl create ns mtls-test
kubectl label ns mtls-test istio-injection=enabled
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: PeerAuthentication; metadata: {name: strict, namespace: mtls-test}
spec: {mtls: {mode: STRICT}}
EOF
kubectl run a --image=nginx -n mtls-test; kubectl run b --image=nginx -n mtls-test
istioctl authn tls-check a -n mtls-test
Lab 4.6
⏱️ 6 min — Image Digest Pinning
Deploy a pod using image tag nginx:latest. Find its digest with kubectl get pod -o json. Update the deployment to use the digest instead of the tag. Verify the pod uses the digest.
Show Solution
Solution
kubectl create deploy nginx --image=nginx:latest
DIGEST=$(kubectl get pod -l app=nginx -o jsonpath='{.items[0].status.containerStatuses[0].imageID}' | cut -d'@' -f2)
kubectl set image deploy/nginx nginx=nginx@$DIGEST
kubectl get deploy nginx -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}'  # Must show @sha256
Lab 4.7
⏱️ 8 min — Kyverno: Disallow Privileged Pods
Install Kyverno. Create a ClusterPolicy that rejects any pod with privileged: true. Test: deploy a privileged pod — must be REJECTED. Deploy a non-privileged pod — must succeed.
Show Solution
Solution
kubectl apply -f https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/releases/latest/download/install.yaml
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1; kind: ClusterPolicy; metadata: {name: disallow-privileged}
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  rules:
  - name: no-privileged; match: {any: [{resources: {kinds: [Pod]}}]}
    validate: {message: "Privileged pods are not allowed", pattern: {spec: {containers: [{securityContext: {privileged: false}}]}}}
EOF
Lab 4.8
⏱️ 6 min — NetworkPolicy Egress Lockdown
Create NetworkPolicy that allows pods labeled app: web to ONLY communicate with: DNS (UDP 53), pods labeled app: db on port 5432. Block everything else. Verify: web pod CANNOT curl google.com.
Show Solution
Solution
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1; kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata: {name: egress-lockdown, namespace: default}
spec:
  podSelector: {app: web}; policyTypes: [Egress]
  egress:
  - to: [{namespaceSelector: {matchLabels: {name: kube-system}}, podSelector: {k8s-app: kube-dns}}]; ports: [{protocol: UDP, port: 53}]
  - to: [{podSelector: {app: db}}]; ports: [{protocol: TCP, port: 5432}]
Lab 4.9
⏱️ 12 min — Vault Integration
Install Vault in dev mode. Enable Kubernetes auth. Create a role. Deploy a pod with Vault sidecar that reads a secret from Vault and writes it to a shared volume. Verify the secret appears in the pod.
Show Solution
Solution
helm install vault hashicorp/vault --set server.dev.enabled=true
kubectl exec vault-0 -- vault auth enable kubernetes
kubectl exec vault-0 -- vault write auth/kubernetes/config token_reviewer_jwt="$(cat /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token)" kubernetes_host=https://kubernetes.default.svc
kubectl exec vault-0 -- vault kv put secret/anihpj/db password=secret123
Lab 4.10
⏱️ 6 min — ServiceAccount Token Projection
Deploy a pod with a projected ServiceAccount token with expirationSeconds: 600. Verify the token exists. Wait 11 minutes and verify the token has been rotated (new token, different signature).
Show Solution
Solution
volumes:
- name: token; projected:
    sources: [{serviceAccountToken: {path: token, expirationSeconds: 600, audience: api}}]
containers:
- volumeMounts: [{name: token, mountPath: /var/run/secrets/tokens, readOnly: true}]

📦 Domain 5: Supply Chain Security — 10 Labs (CKS 20%)

Lab 5.1
⏱️ 8 min — Trivy: Scan, Block, Fix
Scan image nginx:1.21 with Trivy. Note CRITICAL CVEs. Update to nginx:1.25-alpine. Rescan. Verify CRITICAL count dropped significantly. Write a CI pipeline step that blocks on CRITICAL with --exit-code 1.
Show Solution
Solution
trivy image --severity CRITICAL nginx:1.21
trivy image --severity CRITICAL nginx:1.25-alpine
# CI step:
trivy image --severity CRITICAL --exit-code 1 $IMAGE  # Fails pipeline if CRITICAL found
Lab 5.2
⏱️ 10 min — Cosign: Keyless Sign + Verify
Generate a test image. Sign it with cosign keyless (COSIGN_EXPERIMENTAL=1). Push to registry. Verify the signature. Then verify with specific OIDC identity. Attempt to verify with wrong identity — must FAIL.
Show Solution
Solution
docker build -t ghcr.io/anihpj/test:v1 .
docker push ghcr.io/anihpj/test:v1
COSIGN_EXPERIMENTAL=1 cosign sign ghcr.io/anihpj/test@sha256:...
cosign verify ghcr.io/anihpj/test@sha256:...
cosign verify --certificate-identity=wrong@email.com ghcr.io/anihpj/test@sha256:...  # MUST fail
Lab 5.3
⏱️ 6 min — SBOM: Generate + Attach
Generate SBOM for an image with syft (spdx-json format). Attach SBOM to the image with cosign attach sbom. Download and verify the SBOM is retrievable.
Show Solution
Solution
syft nginx:latest -o spdx-json > sbom.json
cosign attach sbom --sbom sbom.json nginx@sha256:...
cosign download sbom nginx@sha256:... | jq .  # Verify it's retrievable
Lab 5.4
⏱️ 8 min — kubesec: Score 3→8
Scan a deliberately insecure pod YAML with kubesec (score ~2-3). Fix: add runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, drop ALL caps, Seccomp, resource limits. Rescan. Target score: 8+.
Show Solution
Solution
kubesec scan insecure-pod.yaml  # ~3/10
# Edit: add securityContext fields
kubesec scan hardened-pod.yaml  # ~8+/10
Lab 5.5
⏱️ 10 min — Gatekeeper: Approved Registries Only
Create ConstraintTemplate + Constraint that only allows images from registry.anihpj.com. Test: deploy nginx from Docker Hub — REJECTED. Deploy image from approved registry — ALLOWED.
Show Solution
Solution
package k8sallowedrepos
violation[{"msg": msg}] {
  container := input.review.object.spec.containers[_]
  not startswith(container.image, "registry.anihpj.com/")
  msg := sprintf("disallowed registry: %v", [container.image])
}
Lab 5.6
⏱️ 8 min — conftest: Rego Policy in CI
Write Rego policy that blocks pods without runAsNonRoot. Test with conftest on a pod YAML. Fail the test (pod without runAsNonRoot). Fix the YAML. Pass the test.
Show Solution
Solution
package main
deny[msg] {
  container := input.spec.containers[_]
  not container.securityContext.runAsNonRoot == true
  msg := sprintf("runAsNonRoot must be true for container %v", [container.name])
}
Lab 5.7
⏱️ 6 min — ImagePolicyWebhook Configuration
Create ImagePolicyWebhook config file. Add admission plugin to API server. Verify the webhook is called on pod creation. Test with an allowed image and a denied image.
Show Solution
Solution
# Add to API server: --enable-admission-plugins=...,ImagePolicyWebhook
# --admission-control-config-file=/etc/kubernetes/image-policy.yaml
# Create config file with kubeconfig pointing to webhook backend
Lab 5.8
⏱️ 10 min — kube-linter: Audit Manifests
Scan a directory of Kubernetes manifests with kube-linter. Identify: pods running as root, missing resource limits, privilege escalation allowed. Fix all HIGH severity findings. Rescan — zero HIGH findings.
Show Solution
Solution
kube-linter lint ./manifests/
kube-linter lint ./manifests/ --include "run-as-non-root,no-privileged,read-only-root-fs"
# Fix findings, rescan until clean
Lab 5.9
⏱️ 8 min — SLSA Provenance Verification
Build an image with SLSA provenance (using slsa-github-generator or manual). Verify the provenance with slsa-verifier. Check that the provenance includes: builder ID, source repo, build recipe.
Show Solution
Solution
slsa-verifier verify-image ghcr.io/anihpj/app@sha256:... --source-uri github.com/anihpj/repo
# Verify output shows: builder ID, source commit, build timestamp
Lab 5.10
⏱️ 8 min — Trivy Operator: Continuous Scanning
Install Trivy Operator. Deploy a pod with a known-vulnerable image. Wait for VulnerabilityReport CRD to be created. Check the report for CVEs. Update the image to a patched version. Verify the report clears.
Show Solution
Solution
kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aquasecurity/trivy-operator/main/deploy/static/trivy-operator.yaml
kubectl run vuln --image=nginx:1.21
kubectl get vulnerabilityreport -o wide  # Shows CVEs
kubectl set image deploy/vuln vuln=nginx:1.25-alpine
kubectl get vulnerabilityreport -o wide  # CVEs reduced/different

🔔 Domain 6: Monitoring, Logging & Runtime Security — 8 Labs (CKS 20%)

Lab 6.1
⏱️ 12 min — Falco: Write Rule, Deploy, Trigger, Verify
Write a custom Falco rule detecting cat /etc/shadow inside any container. Save to falco_rules.local.yaml. Validate with --dry-run. Trigger the alert. Verify it appears in /var/log/falco/alerts.log.
Show Solution
Solution
- rule: Read shadow file
  desc: Detect cat /etc/shadow
  condition: spawned_process and proc.name=cat and proc.args contains /etc/shadow and container.id != host
  output: "Shadow file read! (user=%user.name container=%container.name)"
  priority: CRITICAL
  tags: [filesystem, mitre_credential_access]
Lab 6.2
⏱️ 8 min — Falco Exception Rule
A monitoring agent legitimately runs curl every minute, triggering a Falco rule. Write an exception using append:true that excludes this specific container from the rule. Verify the exception works and other curl calls still alert.
Show Solution
Solution
- rule: Launch Suspicious Network Tool in Container
  append: true
  condition: and not container.name = "monitoring-agent"
Lab 6.3
⏱️ 10 min — Audit Log Query: Find Suspicious Activity
Query audit logs for: (a) all Secret reads in the last hour, (b) all failed authentication attempts, (c) any pod exec operations. Use jq. Document the queries as a runbook.
Show Solution
Solution
cat /var/log/kubernetes/audit.log | jq 'select(.objectRef.resource=="secrets" and .verb=="get")'
cat /var/log/kubernetes/audit.log | jq 'select(.responseStatus.code==401)'
cat /var/log/kubernetes/audit.log | jq 'select(.objectRef.subresource=="exec")'
Lab 6.4
⏱️ 15 min — Incident Response Simulation
Falco alerts: "Terminal shell in container prod/app-123". Execute the full IR playbook: (1) verify the alert, (2) contain (NetworkPolicy + cordon), (3) collect forensics (pod YAML, logs, ps, env), (4) eradicate (delete pod + SA), (5) document findings. Time: 15 minutes.
Show Solution
Solution
POD=app-123; NS=prod; DIR=ir-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M); mkdir $DIR
kubectl apply -f deny-all.yaml -n $NS  # Contain
kubectl get pod $POD -n $NS -o yaml > $DIR/pod.yaml
kubectl logs $POD -n $NS --tail=500 > $DIR/logs.txt
kubectl exec $POD -n $NS -- ps aux > $DIR/ps.txt
kubectl delete pod $POD -n $NS; kubectl delete sa app-sa -n $NS
kubectl create sa app-sa -n $NS  # Fresh SA
Lab 6.5
⏱️ 6 min — Falco Dry-Run Validation
Write a Falco rule with a deliberate syntax error. Run falco --dry-run. Observe the error. Fix the syntax. Run --dry-run again — must pass. Restart Falco. Verify the rule is loaded: falco --list | grep your-rule.
Show Solution
Solution
echo "bad: [syntax" >> /etc/falco/falco_rules.local.yaml
falco --dry-run  # FAILS with parser error
vi /etc/falco/falco_rules.local.yaml  # Fix syntax
falco --dry-run  # PASSES
systemctl restart falco && systemctl status falco
Lab 6.6
⏱️ 8 min — Trivy Operator: Deploy + Monitor
Install Trivy Operator. Verify VulnerabilityReport CRDs are created. Check reports for a specific namespace. Identify the pod with the most CRITICAL CVEs. Recommend remediation.
Show Solution
Solution
kubectl apply -f ...trivy-operator.yaml
kubectl get vulnerabilityreports -A
kubectl get vulnerabilityreport -n prod -o json | jq '.items[] | {name: .metadata.labels["trivy-operator.resource.name"], critical: .report.summary.criticalCount}'
Lab 6.7
⏱️ 10 min — Audit Policy: Noise Reduction
Start with an audit policy that logs everything at Metadata level. Disk fills in hours. Add rules to: (a) suppress health checks (/healthz, /readyz), (b) suppress system component reads, (c) keep Secret access at RequestResponse, (d) keep RBAC changes at RequestResponse. Verify log volume drops significantly.
Show Solution
Solution
rules:
- level: None; nonResourceURLs: ["/healthz", "/readyz", "/livez"]
- level: None; users: ["system:kube-proxy", "system:apiserver"]; verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]
- level: RequestResponse; resources: [{group: "", resources: ["secrets"]}, {group: "rbac.authorization.k8s.io", resources: ["*"]}]
- level: Metadata
Lab 6.8
⏱️ 6 min — kube-bench Continuous Monitoring
Create a CronJob that runs kube-bench weekly against all nodes. Results saved to a PVC. Configure alert if any new FAIL appears. Verify the CronJob runs successfully.
Show Solution
Solution
apiVersion: batch/v1; kind: CronJob; metadata: {name: weekly-kube-bench}
spec:
  schedule: "0 3 * * 0"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          containers:
          - name: kube-bench
            image: aquasec/kube-bench:latest
            command: ["kube-bench", "run", "--targets", "master,node"]
          restartPolicy: OnFailure

🔥 TIMED MOCK EXAM — 2 Hours, 17 Tasks, Target 95%+

This mock exam simulates the real CKS experience. Strict rules: (1) 2-hour timer — no pausing, (2) one browser tab for kubernetes.io/docs only, (3) no notes, no AI tools, (4) score yourself using the rubric after each task. Target: 90%+ on this mock = 95%+ on the real exam.

Task 1
⏱️ 10 min — EncryptionConfiguration
Enable encryption at rest for Secrets using aescbc. Generate a 32-byte key. Create EncryptionConfiguration. Update API server manifest (flag + volumeMount + volume). Verify with etcdctl.
Task 2
⏱️ 8 min — NetworkPolicy: Default-Deny + DNS + App Rules
Create namespace exam-prod. Apply default-deny. Then allow: DNS, ingress from gateway→web:8080, egress web→db:5432. Verify blocked paths fail.
Task 3
⏱️ 8 min — RBAC Least Privilege
SA exam-bot in exam-ns: can update Deployments and create Secrets only. Cannot read Secrets, cannot delete anything. Verify with kubectl auth can-i.
Task 4
⏱️ 12 min — etcd Backup & Restore
Snapshot etcd. Create a Secret. Delete it. Restore from snapshot. Verify Secret is recovered.
Task 5
⏱️ 8 min — Audit Policy
Create audit policy logging: Secrets at Metadata, RBAC at RequestResponse, nothing else. Configure API server. Verify audit events appear.
Task 6
⏱️ 8 min — Cluster Upgrade
Upgrade control plane from v1.29 to v1.30. Take etcd snapshot first. Upgrade kubelet on worker01. Verify all nodes Ready.
Task 7
⏱️ 6 min — PSS Restricted
Label namespace exam-secure with enforce=restricted. Fix existing pod that violates it (runs as root). Redeploy successfully.
Task 8
⏱️ 8 min — SecurityContext Hardening
Deploy a pod with the full CKS securityContext: runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRoot, drop ALL caps, RuntimeDefault Seccomp, noPrivilegeEscalation. Add emptyDir for /tmp. Verify immutable + non-root.
Task 9
⏱️ 7 min — Image Scanning
Scan nginx:1.21 with Trivy. Note CRITICAL count. Update to nginx:1.25-alpine. Rescan. Verify CRITICAL count is lower.
Task 10
⏱️ 8 min — Image Signing
Sign an image with cosign (keyless). Verify signature. Verify with specific identity. Attempt verification with wrong identity — must fail.
Task 11
⏱️ 10 min — AppArmor Profile
Write AppArmor profile allowing /app/** and /tmp/**, denying /etc/kubernetes/. Load with apparmor_parser. Apply to pod via annotation. Verify denial works.
Task 12
⏱️ 8 min — Custom Seccomp Profile
Create Seccomp profile blocking mount, unshare, reboot. Save to /var/lib/kubelet/seccomp/. Apply to pod. Verify.
Task 13
⏱️ 10 min — Falco Custom Rule
Write Falco rule detecting wget/curl execution in production namespace. Save to falco_rules.local.yaml. Validate. Trigger and verify alert.
Task 14
⏱️ 6 min — ServiceAccount No-API
Create SA with automountServiceAccountToken: false. Deploy pod. Verify no token mounted. Verify kubectl auth can-i returns "no" for all verbs.
Task 15
⏱️ 5 min — kube-bench Audit
Run kube-bench. Identify FAILs. Fix at least 2 FAILs. Re-run to verify PASS.
Task 16
⏱️ 6 min — TLS Secret + Ingress
Generate self-signed cert for exam.anihpj.com. Create TLS Secret. Create Ingress with TLS. Verify with curl --resolve.
Task 17
⏱️ 10 min — Incident Response
Falco alerts: shell in container. Full IR: contain (NetworkPolicy), forensics (pod YAML + logs + ps), eradicate (delete pod + SA), document findings.
🎯 Mock Exam Scoring
ScoreMeaning
90%+ (15-17 tasks)Ready for 95%+ on real exam. Book it.
75-89% (13-15 tasks)Close. Review weak domains, practice speed drills.
60-74% (10-12 tasks)Need more lab practice. Focus on timed exercises.
Below 60%Re-do all domain labs before attempting mock again.
